questions.question:
Using empirical formula, calculate the mode for the following data.

17, 20, 21, 18, 25, 28, 24, 22, 16, 24, 25, 24
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total terms (n) = 12 and Sum of data = 264

Mean = 264 ÷ 12 = 22

For 12 sorted items, Median = average of 6th and 7th term = (22 + 24) ÷ 2 = 23

Empirical formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Mode = 3 × 23 − 2 × 22 = 69 − 44 = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data set: 17, 20, 21, 18, 25, 28, 24, 22, 16, 24, 25, 24

**Formula Used:**

Mean = Sum of terms ÷ Total number of terms

Median = Average of (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th terms for even 'n'

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

questions.question: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which AB || DC, and E and F are the midpoints of the diagonals AC and BD, respectively. If AB = 14 cm, BC = 73 cm, DC = 90 cm, and AD = 22 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of EF?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **trapezium**, the length of the segment joining the **midpoints of the diagonals** is half the difference of the parallel sides.

Length of **EF** = (**DC** − **AB**) ÷ 2

⇒ **EF** = (90 − 14) ÷ 2

⇒ **EF** = 76 ÷ 2 = 38 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 38 cm.**

**Given:** **AB** = 14 cm, **DC** = 90 cm, **AB** || **DC**, **E** and **F** are midpoints of **AC** and **BD**.

**Formula Used:** Length of segment joining midpoints of diagonals = |a − b| ÷ 2, where a and b are parallel sides.

questions.question: The total surface of a solid right circular cylinder is 372 π cm², and its height is 25 cm. Its volume is equal to (1)/(5) of the volume of a sphere. The surface area (in cm²) of the sphere is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

From **Total Surface Area** of **cylinder**: 2πr(r + 25) = 372π ⇒ r² + 25r − 186 = 0. Solving, r = 6 cm.

**Volume** of **cylinder** = π × 6² × 25 = 900π cm³.

**Volume** of **sphere** = 5 × 900π = 4500π cm³.

Using Vₛₚₕ = (4/3)πR³ = 4500π ⇒ R³ = 3375 ⇒ R = 15 cm.

**Surface area** of **sphere** = 4πR² = 4 × π × 15² = 900π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 900 π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of **cylinder** = 372π cm²

Height (h) of **cylinder** = 25 cm

Volume of **cylinder** (V꜀) = 1/5 × Volume of **sphere** (Vₛ)

**Formula Used:**

TSA of cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πR³

Surface area of sphere = 4πR²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/817052df6b9e3966e322affbc48b596b13e6e4a43684cfcb96848600cc5f399c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πr(r + 25) = 372π

⇒ r² + 25r = 186

⇒ r² + 25r − 186 = 0

⇒ (r + 31)(r − 6) = 0

⇒ r = 6 cm (as r cannot be negative)

⇒ Volume of **cylinder** = π × 6² × 25 = 900π cm³

⇒ Volume of **sphere** = 5 × 900π = 4500π cm³

⇒ (4/3)πR³ = 4500π

⇒ R³ = (4500 × 3) ÷ 4 = 1125 × 3 = 3375

⇒ R = 15 cm

⇒ Surface Area of **sphere** = 4πR² = 4 × π × 15² = 4 × 225π = 900π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 900 π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Properties

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh; Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h); Volume = πr²h.

Sphere Properties

Surface Area = 4πR²; Volume = (4/3)πR³. For a hemisphere, TSA = 3πR².

Volume Ratios

When comparing volumes of different 3D shapes, ensure all dimensions (radius, height) are in the same units before applying the ratio.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 80 kg of rice at a discount of 10% Besides 1 kg rice was offered free to him on the purchase of every 20 kg rice. If he sells the rice at the marked price, his profit percentage will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** of 1 kg rice be 1 unit.

Total rice received = 80 + (80 ÷ 20) × 1 = 80 + 4 = **84 kg**.

Total **Marked Price** of 84 kg rice = 84 units.

Cost Price (CP) for 80 kg at 10% discount = 80 × 0.9 = **72 units**.

Profit % = (84 − 72) ÷ 72 × 100 = 12 ÷ 72 × 100 = 1/6 × 100 = **16(2/3)%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16(2/3)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** MP of 1 kg rice = Rs. 10; Discount = 10%; Free rice = 1 kg for every 20 kg.

**Formulas:** CP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Profit % = (Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48dcf849f4d4ccc1a533db0fc3a95deafc5907908e544d2a2b8f69f9009e5414.png] 

⇒ Total quantity received = 80 kg + (80/20) kg free = **84 kg**.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) for shopkeeper = (80 kg × Rs. 10) × 0.90 = **Rs. 720**.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) at Marked Price = 84 kg × Rs. 10 = **Rs. 840**.

⇒ Profit = 840 − 720 = **Rs. 120**.

⇒ Profit % = (120 ÷ 720) × 100 = 1/6 × 100 = **16(2/3)%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16(2/3)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Free Items Concept

When items are offered free, the effective cost price per unit decreases. Net discount % = [Free items ÷ (Paid items + Free items)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

The shopkeeper receives a double benefit: a direct cash discount and a quantity discount. Total Profit % = [(Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP] × 100.</p

questions.question: A triangular field has sides measuring 42 cm, 34 cm and 20 cm. What is the length of the altitude corresponding to the longest side?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize **Pythagorean Triplets** to split the base 42 cm into two parts: 12 cm and 30 cm.

For side 20 cm, triplet (3, 4, 5) × 4 → (12, **16**, 20).

For side 34 cm, triplet (8, 15, 17) × 2 → (**16**, 30, 34).

Check: 12 + 30 = 42 cm (the longest side). The common height is **16 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sides of the triangle are **a = 42 cm**, **b = 34 cm**, and **c = 20 cm**.

**Formula Used:** Heron's Formula for **Area** = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] and **Area** = 1/2 × base × height.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/818b3a93072e35c0828316e36a3c3b69536481fcca393cfcf20a60fdc666e253.png] 

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (42 + 34 + 20) ÷ 2

⇒ s = 96 ÷ 2 = 48 cm

⇒ Area = √[48 × (48 − 42) × (48 − 34) × (48 − 20)]

⇒ Area = √[48 × 6 × 14 × 28]

⇒ Area = √[(16 × 3) × (3 × 2) × (14) × (14 × 2)]

⇒ Area = √[16 × 3² × 2² × 14²] = 4 × 3 × 2 × 14 = 336 cm²

⇒ For longest side (base = 42 cm), Area = 1/2 × 42 × height

⇒ 336 = 21 × height

⇒ height = 336 ÷ 21 = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of any triangle when all three sides are known: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter.

Altitude vs. Side Length

In any triangle, the **longest side** always has the **shortest altitude** corresponding to it, as Area = 1/2 × b × h remains constant.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers (a, b, c) such that a² + b² = c², helping solve triangle problems quickly without complex calculations.</p

questions.question: Karan was born 3 years after his parent's marriage. His father is 6 years older than his mother but 26 years older than Karan who is 12 years of age as on today. At what age did his mother get married?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Karan** is 12 years old.

**Father's** current age = 12 + 26 = 38 years.

**Mother's** current age = 38 − 6 = 32 years.

**Karan** was born 3 years after marriage → Marriage was 12 + 3 = 15 years ago.

**Mother's age at marriage** = 32 − 15 = 17 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f7ecfcea0bfbb842161bfaff502617f40e69c33b69602303c4ca40780588d1d.png] 

**Given:**

**Karan's** current age = 12 years.

**Father's** age = **Karan's** age + 26 years.

**Mother's** age = **Father's** age − 6 years.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Father's** current age = 12 + 26 = 38 years.

⇒ **Mother's** current age = 38 − 6 = 32 years.

⇒ Total years since marriage = **Karan's** age + Years after marriage Karan was born.

⇒ Total years since marriage = 12 + 3 = 15 years.

⇒ **Mother's age at marriage** = Current Age − Years since marriage.

⇒ **Mother's age at marriage** = 32 − 15 = 17 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Age Difference Consistency

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** throughout their lives. If the father is 6 years older than the mother today, he was also 6 years older at the time of marriage.

Linear Equations in Ages

Age problems can be solved by setting a variable (usually **x**) for the present age and subtracting/adding for past or future scenarios (x − n or x + n).

Ratio of Ages

Unlike the age difference, the **ratio** of ages of two individuals changes every year as they grow older.</p

questions.question: A sum of money invested at a certain rate of simple interest per annum amounts to Rs. 14,522 in seven years and to Rs. 18,906 in eleven years. Find the sum invested (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 4 years (11 − 7) = 18906 − 14522 = ₹4384

Interest for 1 year = 4384 ÷ 4 = ₹1096

Interest for 7 years = 1096 × 7 = ₹7672

**Sum (Principal)** = Amount₇yᵣ − Interest₇yᵣ = 14522 − 7672 = ₹6850

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6850.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount in 7 years (A₇) = ₹14,522

Amount in 11 years (A₁₁) = ₹18,906

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = **Principal (P)** + **Simple Interest (SI)**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/847b440a057b911d15d4932e562b747d7fa13ca9fdd50971f0bb0640d20d2946.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest for 4 years = A₁₁ − A₇

⇒ Interest for 4 years = 18906 − 14522 = ₹4384

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 4384 ÷ 4 = ₹1096

⇒ Simple Interest for 7 years = 1096 × 7 = ₹7672

⇒ Principal (P) = Amount after 7 years − Interest for 7 years

⇒ P = 14522 − 7672

⇒ P = ₹6850

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6850.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Nature

In Simple Interest, the interest remains **constant** for every year as it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Rate of Interest Formula

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T). In this case, R = (1096 × 100) ÷ (6850 × 1) = 16%.

Difference between CI and SI

For a period of 2 years, the difference is given by P(R ÷ 100)².

questions.question: In a ΔPMN, ∠P = 76°. The bisectors of the exterior angles at M and N intersect each other at point O. The degree measure of ∠MON is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the **bisectors** of two **exterior angles** of a **triangle** is given by the direct formula:

∠MON = 90° − ∠P ÷ 2

Given, ∠P = 76°

∠MON = 90° − 76° ÷ 2 = 90° − 38° = 52°

**∴ The correct answer is 52°.**

questions.question: A man bought 2 articles for Rs. 3050 each. He sold one article at 10% loss and another at 20% profit. The total profit/loss percentage he earned is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the **Cost Price (CP)** of two articles is the **same**, the net profit or loss percentage is the **arithmetic mean** of the individual profit/loss percentages.

Net Profit/Loss % = (Percentage 1 + Percentage 2) ÷ 2

Net % = (−10% + 20%) ÷ 2 = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%

Since the result is **positive**, it is a **profit**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5% profit.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of Article 1 = ₹3050

CP of Article 2 = ₹3050

Loss on Article 1 = 10%

Profit on Article 2 = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss %) ÷ 100

Profit % = (Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17587968226e9c02cc8b589b9473304bbecf3b8b9c61a57b961032c057f73ce0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 3050 + 3050 = ₹6100

⇒ SP₁ = 3050 × (90 ÷ 100) = ₹2745

⇒ SP₂ = 3050 × (120 ÷ 100) = ₹3660

⇒ Total SP = 2745 + 3660 = ₹6405

⇒ Net Profit = 6405 − 6100 = ₹305

⇒ Net Profit % = (305 ÷ 6100) × 100

⇒ Net Profit % = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5% profit.**

**__Additional Information__**

Same Selling Price Case

If two articles are sold at the **same Selling Price (SP)**, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, there is always a net loss of (x/10)² %.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit % and Loss % are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise in the question.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is given by [a + b + (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

questions.question: A local train without stoppages runs at an average speed of 88 km/hr, and with stoppages, at an average speed of 24 km/hr. What is the total time (in hours) taken by the local train for stoppages on a route of length 528 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Stoppage time per hour** = (Difference in speed ÷ Faster speed)

**Stoppage time per hour** = (88 − 24) ÷ 88 = 64 ÷ 88 = 8/11 hours

**Total travel time (with stoppages)** = Distance ÷ Speed with stoppages = 528 ÷ 24 = 22 hours

**Total stoppage time** = 22 × (8/11) = 2 × 8 = 16 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e37dd7306092924e8673475669cad5badd518e760a026ea8f85211b7c7ae4f57.png] 
**Given:**

Average speed without stoppages = 88 km/hr

Average speed with stoppages = 24 km/hr

Total distance = 528 km

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken without stoppages = Distance ÷ Speed = 528 ÷ 88

⇒ Time taken without stoppages = 6 hours

⇒ Time taken with stoppages = Distance ÷ Speed = 528 ÷ 24

⇒ Time taken with stoppages = 22 hours

⇒ Total stoppage time = Time (with stops) − Time (without stops)

⇒ Total stoppage time = 22 − 6 = 16 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Stoppage Time Calculation

The formula for stoppage time per hour is: (Sfₐₛₜ − Sₛₗₒw) ÷ Sfₐₛₜ. Multiply this by total travel time to get absolute stoppage time.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. Stoppages reduce the average speed because they increase the total time taken for the same distance.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: Two trains are running on opposite tracks between stations A and B. After crossing each other they take 4 hr and 9 hr respectively to reach their destination. If speed of first train is 54 kmph, find the speed of second train.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two objects starting at the same time from opposite points, the relation after they cross is **S₁ / S₂ = √(T₂ / T₁)**.

Here, S₁ = 54 kmph, T₁ = 4 hr, and T₂ = 9 hr.

54 / S₂ = √(9 / 4) = 3 / 2

S₂ = (54 × 2) / 3 = 36 kmph.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kmph.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the **first train** (S₁) = 54 kmph

Time taken by the first train after crossing to reach **Station B** (T₁) = 4 hr

Time taken by the **second train** after crossing to reach **Station A** (T₂) = 9 hr

**Formula Used:**

The ratio of the speeds of two trains is inversely proportional to the square root of the time taken by them to reach their destinations after meeting.

S₁ / S₂ = √(T₂ / T₁)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfb9bfad5561cdd54321707af4645c2def54684885cee069d442269de4198452.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 54 / S₂ = √(9 / 4)

⇒ 54 / S₂ = 3 / 2

⇒ 3 × S₂ = 54 × 2

⇒ 3 × S₂ = 108

⇒ S₂ = 108 / 3

⇒ S₂ = 36 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kmph.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting Time Formula

The time taken to meet for the first time is **Distance / (S₁ + S₂)** if they start simultaneously.

Speed Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 minutes. Another pipe can empty that tank in 30 minutes. If both are opened alternatively, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 20, 30) = 60 units.

Efficiency: A = +3, B = −2. Net work in 2 mins = 1 unit.

To avoid overflow, subtract filling capacity: 60 − 3 = 57 units.

Time for 57 units = 57 × 2 = 114 mins.

Remaining 3 units filled by A in 3/3 = 1 min.

Total time = 114 + 1 = 115 mins.

**∴ The correct answer is 115.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Filling Pipe (A) = 20 mins, Emptying Pipe (B) = 30 mins.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Pipes
 Time
 Quantity
 Efficiency
 
 

 A (fill)
 20
 
 60
 
 +3
 
 

 B (empty)
 30
 −2
 
 

⇒ Total capacity = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units.

⇒ 1st minute: Pipe A fills 3 units.

⇒ 2nd minute: Pipe B empties 2 units.

⇒ Net work in 1 cycle (2 minutes) = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

⇒ Remaining work for last filling step = 60 − 3 = 57 units.

⇒ Time taken to reach 57 units = 57 cycles × 2 minutes/cycle = 114 minutes.

⇒ Work remaining = 60 − 57 = 3 units.

⇒ This 3 units will be filled by Pipe A in next minute: 3 ÷ 3 = 1 minute.

⇒ Total time taken = 114 + 1 = 115 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 115.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Efficiency Concept

In Pipes and Cisterns, an inlet pipe has positive efficiency (+) while an outlet or leak pipe has negative efficiency (−).

Alternate Work Rule

When filling and emptying alternately, the tank is considered full as soon as the filling pipe completes the work. Always subtract the filling efficiency from the total capacity before calculating cycles.

Pipes & Cisterns Formula

Net Work done = (Sum of inlet efficiencies − Sum of outlet efficiencies) × Time.</p

questions.question: The largest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 88 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**88** is a multiple of **8** and **11**.

Check options for **divisibility by 11** (difference of sum of digits at odd and even places is 0 or 11).

9944: (9+4) − (9+4) = 0 (Divisible by 11). Check **divisibility by 8**: 944 ÷ 8 = 118 (Divisible by 8).

Since 9944 is the largest among valid options, it is the answer.

**∴ The correct answer is 9944.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisor = 88, Target = **Largest 4-digit number**.

**Formula Used:** Required Number = Largest number − Remainder
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce6237630fb75e2724313a2e88afcbcf67091bedf31da3218aa57974d1a9a24a.png] 
⇒ **Largest 4-digit number** = 9999

⇒ Divide 9999 by 88:

⇒ 9999 = 88 × 113 + 55

⇒ **Remainder** = 55

⇒ **Largest divisible number** = 9999 − 55

⇒ **Largest divisible number** = 9944

**∴ The correct answer is 9944.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8 or are zeros.

Divisibility Rule of 11

Subtract the sum of digits in even positions from the sum of digits in odd positions. If the result is 0 or divisible by 11, the number is divisible by 11.

Composite Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers (like 8 and 11), it is also divisible by their product (88).</p

questions.question: The cost of a washing machine is 40% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 52% and that of the TV decreases by 76%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 5 washing machines and 2 TVs?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **TV** cost = 100. Then **Washing Machine (WM)** cost = 60.

Initial total cost of 5 **WM** and 2 **TV** = (5 × 60) + (2 × 100) = 300 + 200 = 500.

New **WM** cost = 60 × 1.52 = 91.2 | New **TV** cost = 100 × 0.24 = 24.

New total cost = (5 × 91.2) + (2 × 24) = 456 + 48 = 504.

% Change = (504 − 500) ÷ 500 × 100 = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increase by 0.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f962dcb28934fba53745b0b7087b30eb442a1638087b883a9550d146629464e.png] 

**Given:** **Cost Price (CP)** of **Washing Machine** = 60% of **TV**.

⇒ Let **CP** of **TV** = ₹100; **CP** of **Washing Machine** = ₹60.

⇒ Initial cost of 5 **WM** and 2 **TV** = (5 × 60) + (2 × 100) = 300 + 200 = ₹500.

⇒ New **CP** of **WM** = 60 + (52% of 60) = 60 + 31.2 = ₹91.2.

⇒ New **CP** of **TV** = 100 − (76% of 100) = ₹24.

⇒ New total cost for 5 **WM** and 2 **TV** = (5 × 91.2) + (2 × 24) = 456 + 48 = ₹504.

⇒ Increase in total cost = 504 − 500 = ₹4.

⇒ Percentage Change = (4 ÷ 500) × 100 = 0.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increase by 0.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase/Decrease

The percentage change is calculated as: [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Weighted Average Method

When components of a group change by different percentages, the net change is the weighted average of individual percentage changes.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes x% and y%, the effective change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of equation x² – 2x + 4 = 0, then what is the equation whose roots are α³/β² and β³/α²?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For the equation x² − 2x + 4 = 0, the sum α + β = 2 and product αβ = 4.

Multiplying by (α + 2), we get α³ + 2³ = 0 ⇒ α³ = −8. Similarly, β³ = −8.

New root 1: α³/β² = −8/β². Since β = 4/α, Root 1 = −8 ÷ (16/α²) = −α²/2.

From the original equation: α² = 2α − 4 ⇒ −α²/2 = −(2α − 4)/2 = 2 − α. Since α + β = 2, then 2 − α = β.

The new roots are simply β and α, making the new equation identical to the original.

**∴ The correct answer is x² − 2x + 4 = 0.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given equation: x² − 2x + 4 = 0

Sum of roots (α + β) = 2

Product of roots (αβ) = 4

To find the equation with roots p = α³/β² and q = β³/α²:

⇒ Sum (S) = p + q = α³/β² + β³/α² = (α⁵ + β⁵) / (αβ)²

⇒ α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 2² − 2(4) = 4 − 8 = −4

⇒ α³ + β³ = (α + β)(α² + β² − αβ) = 2(−4 − 4) = −16

⇒ α⁵ + β⁵ = (α² + β²)(α³ + β³) − α²β²(α + β)

⇒ α⁵ + β⁵ = (−4)(−16) − (4²)(2) = 64 − 32 = 32

⇒ S = 32 / 4² = 32 / 16 = 2

⇒ Product (P) = p × q = (α³/β²) × (β³/α²) = αβ = 4

⇒ Required equation: x² − Sx + P = 0

⇒ x² − 2x + 4 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is x² − 2x + 4 = 0.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Roots and Coefficients

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.

Formation of Quadratic Equation

If the roots are p and q, the quadratic equation is given by x² − (p + q)x + pq = 0.

Complex Roots of Unity

Equations of the form x² ± ax + a² = 0 have roots related to the cube roots of −a³ or a³, involving terms like aω and aω².

Newton's Sums for Powers

Higher powers of roots can be found using the relation Sₙ = αⁿ + βⁿ, where aSₙ + bSₙ−₁ + cSₙ−₂ = 0.</p

questions.question: A straight vertical pole was broken during a cyclone in such a way that its top touched the ground at a distance of 6sqrt 3 m from the bottom of the pole and made and angle of 30° with the horizontal. What was the height (in m) of the pole?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°-60°-90°** triangle, the side ratios are **1 : √3 : 2**.

Distance from base (√3 part) = 6√3 m ⇒ 1 unit = 6 m.

Height of broken part (1 unit) = 6 m and Hypotenuse (2 units) = 12 m.

Total height of **vertical pole** = 6 + 12 = 18 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3eb7e80e74a742c56d4abc107331ea0efe2ecace20019979a21be259dc4f678c.png] 

**Given:** Distance BC = 6√3 m, Angle of elevation θ = 30°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular/Base; cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse.

⇒ In triangle ABC, tan 30° = AB / BC

⇒ 1/√3 = AB / 6√3

⇒ AB = 6 m (Height of standing part)

⇒ cos 30° = BC / AC

⇒ √3/2 = 6√3 / AC

⇒ AC = 12 m (Length of broken part)

⇒ Total height of pole = AB + AC = 6 + 12 = 18 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Common values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Height and Distance

The total height of a **broken object** is the sum of the vertical segment and the slant hypotenuse segment.

Standard Triangle Proportions

For a 30° angle, the ratio of Height : Base : Hypotenuse is always 1 : √3 : 2.</p

questions.question: A bag contains 1-rupee and 2-rupee coins. The total number of coins is 10, and their total value is ₹16. What is the difference between the numbers of two-rupee coins and one-rupee coins?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using **Alligation** method on average coin value:

Average value per coin = 16 ÷ 10 = ₹1.6

Ratio of 1-rupee coins to 2-rupee coins = (2 − 1.6) : (1.6 − 1) = 0.4 : 0.6 = 2 : 3

Total ratio units (2 + 3) = 5 → 10 coins. So, 1 unit = 2 coins.

Difference in units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit × 2 = 2 coins.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total coins = 10, Total value = ₹16.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36a6112185ff066b1dff281ec3d9280eeb1af4a297d2233e5bf25e19f0843da4.png] 

Let the number of **1-rupee coins** be x and **2-rupee coins** be y.

⇒ x + y = 10 ... (i)

⇒ 1 × x + 2 × y = 16 ⇒ x + 2y = 16 ... (ii)

Subtracting equation (i) from (ii):

⇒ (x + 2y) − (x + y) = 16 − 10

⇒ y = 6

Substituting y = 6 in (i):

⇒ x + 6 = 10 ⇒ x = 4

Difference between the numbers of coins:

⇒ |6 − 4| = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixture and Alligation in Coins

This technique allows solving linear equations by finding the ratio of quantities when their weighted average is known.

Linear Equations in Two Variables

For coin problems, use equations: x + y = Total Quantity and (Value₁ × x) + (Value₂ × y) = Total Value.

questions.question: A and B will take 3 more days and 12 more days than the number of days they require to finish the same work working together. Find the number of days in which A can make the painting alone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the time taken by **A and B together** be **x** days.

When A takes **a** extra days and B takes **b** extra days than together, the formula is **x = √(a × b)**.

Given **a = 3** and **b = 12**, we get **x = √(3 × 12) = √36 = 6** days.

Time taken by **A alone** = Together time + Extra days = 6 + 3 = **9 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Extra days for **A** = 3 days | Extra days for **B** = 12 days.

**Formula Used:**

If A takes (x + a) days and B takes (x + b) days to do work that they do together in x days, then 1/(x + a) + 1/(x + b) = 1/x.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 9
 18 (LCM)
 2
 
 

 B
 18
 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let **A + B** together take **x** days.

⇒ Time for **A** = (x + 3) days

⇒ Time for **B** = (x + 12) days

⇒ 1/(x + 3) + 1/(x + 12) = 1/x

⇒ [(x + 12) + (x + 3)] / [(x + 3)(x + 12)] = 1/x

⇒ (2x + 15) / (x² + 15x + 36) = 1/x

⇒ 2x² + 15x = x² + 15x + 36

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = 6

⇒ **A alone** = x + 3 = 6 + 3 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root Trick for Extra Days

When two people take 'a' and 'b' days more than their combined time 'x', the combined time is always x = √(a × b).

Work and Efficiency Relation

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to **Time**. If the ratio of time is x : y, the ratio of efficiency is y : x.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept applies to **Pipes and Cisterns** where an inlet pipe has positive efficiency and an outlet pipe has negative efficiency.

LCM Method

Total work can be assumed as the **LCM** of individual days to simplify calculations into integer efficiency values.</p

questions.question: The surface area of three faces of a cuboid sharing a vertex are 20 m², 32 m² and 40 m². What is the volume of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **Volume (V)** of a cuboid with areas of three **adjacent faces** x, y, and z is given by the formula: **V = √(x × y × z)**.

Given adjacent face areas: x = 20 m², y = 32 m², and z = 40 m².

⇒ Volume = √(20 × 32 × 40)

⇒ Volume = √25600 = 160 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 160 m³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of face 1 (l × b) = 20 m²

Area of face 2 (b × h) = 32 m²

Area of face 3 (l × h) = 40 m²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97bc0fa0efea05a40aa7e368dcdc4ac264ec219e48d95fd29ebce8abbaf23422.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cuboid (V) = length (l) × breadth (b) × height (h)

Product of areas of three adjacent faces = (l × b) × (b × h) × (l × h) = l²b²h² = (lbh)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (lbh)² = 20 × 32 × 40

⇒ (lbh)² = 640 × 40

⇒ (lbh)² = 25600

⇒ lbh = √25600

⇒ lbh = 160

**∴ The correct answer is 160 m³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area is the sum of the areas of all 6 faces: TSA = 2(lb + bh + lh).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its diagonal: d = √(l² + b² + h²).

Volume of a Cube

For a cube, length = breadth = height = a. Therefore, Volume = a³ and Surface Area = 6a².</p

questions.question: The total population of a town is 5500. The number of males and females increases by 5% and 10% respectively and resulting population becomes 6000. Find the number of men in the town.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **increase** in population = 6000 − 5500 = 500.

Assume all 5500 were **males**: Increase = 5% of 5500 = 275.

Assume all 5500 were **females**: Increase = 10% of 5500 = 550.

By **Alligation** on increase values: (550 − 500) : (500 − 275) = 50 : 225 = 2 : 9.

Number of **men** = (2 / 11) × 5500 = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **total population** = 5500, **Final population** = 6000, **Male increase** = 5%, **Female increase** = 10%.

**Formula Used:** Total Increase = (Increase% of Males) + (Increase% of Females)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e3c72731cee7293f9d66f1fbb1cb61373dfb12c8feaa03375697b1db088a32.png] 

Let the number of **males** be x and **females** be (5500 − x).

⇒ 5% of x + 10% of (5500 − x) = 500

⇒ 0.05x + 0.10(5500 − x) = 500

⇒ 0.05x + 550 − 0.10x = 500

⇒ −0.05x = 500 − 550

⇒ −0.05x = −50

⇒ x = 50 / 0.05

⇒ x = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Original Value) / Original Value] × 100.

Alligation Method in Population

Ratio of two groups = (Higher % change − Average % change) : (Average % change − Lower % change).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%.</p

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is one-twentieth of their LCM. If one of the numbers is 96 and the difference of the LCM and the HCF is 456, then what is the other number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let HCF = 1 unit and LCM = 20 units.

Difference between LCM and HCF = 20 − 1 = 19 units.

Given 19 units = 456 ⇒ 1 unit (HCF) = 24.

LCM = 20 × 24 = 480.

Other Number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ First Number = (24 × 480) ÷ 96 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (n₁) = 96

HCF = LCM ÷ 20

LCM − HCF = 456

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2df10b69cfc840a9c0ccfad4073681e2cdb281fef1269ce04e706b53af84b3d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let LCM = L and HCF = H.

⇒ H = L ÷ 20 ⇒ L = 20H.

⇒ L − H = 456

⇒ 20H − H = 456

⇒ 19H = 456

⇒ H = 456 ÷ 19 = 24.

⇒ L = 20 × 24 = 480.

⇒ Let the other number be n₂.

⇒ n₁ × n₂ = H × L

⇒ 96 × n₂ = 24 × 480

⇒ n₂ = (24 × 480) ÷ 96

⇒ n₂ = 480 ÷ 4 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule

For any two numbers a and b, the relationship is always: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Divisibility Property

The HCF of any set of numbers is always a factor of their LCM.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their HCF is 1 and their LCM is equal to their product.</p

questions.question: Out of 6 numbers, the sum of the first 5 numbers is 7 times the 6th number. If their average is 136, then the 6th number is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Sum of first 5 numbers** to the **6th number** = 7 : 1

Total ratio parts = 7 + 1 = 8 parts

Total sum of 6 numbers = **Average** × 6 = 136 × 6

Value of 1 part (6th number) = (136 × 6) ÷ 8 = 17 × 6 = 102

**∴ The correct answer is 102.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Average** of 6 numbers = 136, **Sum** of first 5 = 7 × 6th number.

**Formula Used:** Total Sum = Average × Number of items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7b24195c15ba5f6e0743ede1e8a42e967e6c1f49198fffbcaf6d05177f0dc7f.png] 

⇒ Let the **6th number** be x.

⇒ Sum of the **first 5 numbers** = 7x.

⇒ Total sum of all 6 numbers = 7x + x = 8x.

⇒ According to the average formula, 8x = 136 × 6.

⇒ 8x = 816

⇒ x = 816 ÷ 8

⇒ x = 102

**∴ The correct answer is 102.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The **average** of n numbers is calculated as (Sum of all n numbers) ÷ n. Conversely, Sum = Average × n.

Weighted Average

If two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Effect of Change

If every number in a set is **increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided** by a constant k, the **new average** will also be increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by k respectively.</p

questions.question: If x+(1)/(x)=sqrt{13}, then one of the values x³-(1)/(x³) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = k, then x − 1/x = √(k² − 4).

Here, k = √13, so x − 1/x = √(13 − 4) = √9 = 3.

If x − 1/x = a, then x³ − 1/x³ = a³ + 3a.

Substituting a = 3, we get: 3³ + 3 × 3 = 27 + 9 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 1/x = √13

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = (x + 1/x)² − 4(x)(1/x)

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = (√13)² − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 13 − 4 = 9

⇒ x − 1/x = ±3

Taking x − 1/x = 3 (since the positive value matches the given options):

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)³ + 3(x)(1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 3³ + 3 × 3

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 27 + 9 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2. This is derived directly from expanding the whole square formula (x + 1/x)².

Difference of Squares Transition

The relationship between the sum and difference of reciprocal terms is given by the identity (x + 1/x)² − (x − 1/x)² = 4.

Sum of Cubes Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k. This comes from rearranging the expansion of (x + 1/x)³.

Difference of Cubes Identity

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k. This is an essential shortcut for quickly solving differences of cubed terms in algebra.
</p

questions.question: If sec θ + tan θ = 5, then Sin θ = ______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **sec θ + tan θ = k**, then **sec θ − tan θ = 1/k**.

Given k = 5, then sec θ − tan θ = 1/5.

Adding both: 2 sec θ = 5 + 1/5 = 26/5 ⇒ sec θ = 13/5.

Using **triplet (5, 12, 13)**: If Hypotenuse = 13 and Base = 5, then Perpendicular = 12.

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse = 12/13.

**∴ The correct answer is 12/13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4622aa72b57e067f70ad03c4aeb23fa0afb88c9e548a003f52b87ec7b9e53912.png] 

**Given:** sec θ + tan θ = 5 --- (i)

**Formula Used:** sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

⇒ (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1

⇒ 5 × (sec θ − tan θ) = 1

⇒ sec θ − tan θ = 1/5 --- (ii)

⇒ Adding (i) and (ii): 2 sec θ = 5 + 0.2 = 5.2

⇒ sec θ = 2.6 = 26/10 = 13/5

⇒ Since sec θ = Hypotenuse / Base, let H = 13 and B = 5.

⇒ P = √(H² − B²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12

⇒ sin θ = P / H = 12/13

**∴ The correct answer is 12/13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Standard identities include sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets used in exams: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), (8, 15, 17), and (9, 40, 41).

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1/cos θ and tan θ = sin θ/cos θ. If sec θ + tan θ = x, then sec θ = (x² + 1)/2x and tan θ = (x² − 1)/2x.</p
